notes: Terraqueous Globe - Natural Earth II, stated in the map's own legend ('Compromise pseudocylindrical projection Natural Earth II') and confirmed by measurement. S2 REPLACED S1's hand-picked feature control points with exact graticule crossings: the oval's drawn boundary curve was traced across 2001 rows and the NE-II envelope least-squares fitted to it, giving centre (1999.55, 1129.29), scale sx=702.212 sy=702.683, inlier RMS 0.363 px with every traced row inside 10 px. Two independent checks pass - sx/sy = 0.99933 (isotropic, i.e. drawn to true NE-II proportions, which a wrong polynomial could not produce alongside a sub-pixel envelope fit), and the fitted graticule lands within ~2 px of the map's own printed degree labels (170W at x=234, measured 236; equator y=1129, measured 1130; 20S y=1378, measured 1377). The control points below are that fit evaluated at named graticule crossings, so reproject.py recovers the same four constants from them. Crop is the oval interior, inset ~4 px from the drawn boundary rule so the black envelope line is never sampled; the generator clamps into the crop rather than masking, because the canvas seam at lon +-180 lands exactly on that rule. The polar insets (from y=2148) and the title/legend block sit outside it. Highest coastline precedence: this is the only whole-world source registered to sub-pixel accuracy, so it - not the regional relief - defines the shoreline.
